text:
I tested all five pages with scripted DOM checks, a screenshot and one live interaction, but I did not do a full keyboard walkthrough. Anything I couldn't confirm is marked NEEDS_REVIEW.

**Findings that drive the FAIL results**
- **Search page, 1.3.1:** several filter inputs share the same `id` (`id_filter_search`, `id_filter_sort_by_1`, and their clear and submit buttons). The visible "Search" labels all bind to the first input, so the others have no programmatically associated label. They only carry an `aria-label` of "Search...".
- **Search page, 3.2.2:** ticking one filter checkbox changed the URL and reloaded the results with no submit button and no advance warning.
- **CI Lab page, 2.1.1:** the demo reel `<video id="demo-reel">` has no `controls`. Its only play affordance is the poster image, and nothing keyboard-focusable starts it.

**Things for a person to check**
- **Home carousel, 2.2.2:** `#home_page_carousel` is set to auto-advance every 7.5 seconds and has no pause control. It did not advance during my 9-second test, so I couldn't confirm it.
- **Home page, 2.1.1:** the links and buttons in the "Recently released" gallery are all `tabindex="-1"`. I couldn't tell whether they are reachable by keyboard another way.
- **Home page, 3.2.2:** the filter checkboxes there probably update results on change like the search page does, but I didn't test it.
- **Search page, 4.1.2:** the sort select's accessible name is "Sort category", while its visible label is "Sort by:".
- **No skip link on any page:** the SVS pages have `<main>` and headings, which I took as meeting 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks). The CI Lab page has no landmarks or headings, so I left it for review.
- **Search box labels, 3.3.2:** the navbar search box shows only placeholder text, so a person should judge whether that counts as a visible label.

I only measured focus visibility on the home page, where no focusable element lost its outline. The other pages got NEEDS_REVIEW for 2.4.7. The error criteria (3.3.1, 3.3.3, 3.3.4) are DNA because none of the pages has a form that validates input or runs a transaction.
